introduction: [FATHER_NAME] is a Vedic astrologer. His work is with one person, and one chart, at a time. The aim is to explain a classical system in language that can be followed without special training, and to leave the decisions where they belong: with the person who asked.
passion: Astrology, for him, is a long study rather than a performance. The interest is in the grammar of the chart — signs, houses, and planetary periods — and in the person who has come with a real question.
philosophy: A chart is a language, not a finished sentence. It can describe tendencies and timings as the tradition understands them. It does not replace a person's judgment, and it is not a substitute for medical, legal, or financial advice.
approach: Consultations begin with listening. The reading stays with the questions that were brought into the room, and the explanation is paced so it can be repeated later to a spouse, a parent, or to oneself.

points.title: Traditional astrology knowledge
points.text: Readings stay with classical Vedic methods, and the technique being used is named rather than mixed in silently with other systems.

points.title: Personal attention
points.text: Each sitting is arranged for one person or one family question. The chart is read for that conversation, not from a generic script.

points.title: Detailed explanations
points.text: Placements and periods are explained in ordinary language, with room to ask what a word means before the reading moves on.

points.title: Confidential consultations
points.text: What is shared in a consultation is private. Family matters, dates of birth, and personal questions are not material for publicity.

points.title: Easy-to-understand guidance
points.text: The point of the hour is that you leave able to retell the explanation. Jargon is translated, not used as decoration.

points.title: Respectful and patient communication
points.text: Questions are welcome, including disagreement. A consultation is a conversation between adults, conducted without pressure or fear.
